subject: Post-demo: Forecasting commit probability & approval path
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@harborhealth.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Forecasting commit probability & approval path

Hi Samir / Lena — great to run through the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few asks so we can map this to your procurement windows: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary pilot scope: conversational QA + summarization for two clinical workflows (triage & discharge notes).
- Expected token profile: short prompts, average 100 tokens/request; projected call volume ~1.2M requests/month -> ~120M tokens/month (midpoint).
- Range that leadership mentioned: 60M — 240M tokens/month depending on adoption speed.

Cost & unit economics next steps
- You asked for a simple $/1M-token band to present to finance. Based on the model we covered, rough target band to aim for: $380 — $520 per 1M tokens depending on batching, KV cache hit rates, and quantization (this is a working range; SE will run tighter scenarios).
- Procurement thresholds you flagged: PO approval required for vendor spend >$75k/month; finance prefers 3 quotes for any multi-month commitment.

Immediate asks / action items
1) Can you confirm the internal procurement contact and whether the $75k/month PO threshold is firm? (Samir indicated procurement may allow pilot exceptions.)
2) Decision timeline: what’s a realistic window for a pilot approval? You mentioned end-of-Q4 could be possible but wanted to confirm.
3) I attached a simple budget model (harbor_budget_model.xlsx) — we filled in the midpoint numbers we discussed. Please iterate it with your finance team and send back a version if you want us to tune assumptions.

Proposed next steps from Redwood
- SE will provide a concise per-1M-token summary and a 3-tier pricing table for pilot vs committed volume.
- We’ll propose a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones (pilot kickoff, success metrics, procurement signoff).

If you want, I can schedule a brief call with our procurement lead and legal (10–15m) to walk the procurement path options.

Thanks — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz

Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Forecasting commit probability & approval path

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap and the model. A few quick clarifications from my side: 

1) Procurement / PO thresholds
- $75k/month is the standard threshold where procurement requires a formal RFP/3-quote process; we can do an exception for a limited pilot but it needs an exec sponsor and finance signoff.
- Typical procurement lead time for exceptions is 6–8 weeks (legal + finance review).

2) Decision timing & probability
- My read is that a 3-month pilot starting mid-November is realistic if we can show a simple cost projection and pilot SOW by next week.
- Current internal probability: ~40% for a formal pilot commit (assuming price hits ~$400/1M tokens or better for the pilot).

3) What we need from Redwood
- A one-page cost summary (simple table: low/mid/high monthly tokens -> $/1M -> monthly $).
- A short pilot commercial option (pilot at a discounted unit rate or prepay credit).

I’ve looped in Lena (Finance) to validate PO threshold and to surface any additional constraints. She’ll push this to procurement if we get a clean pricing sheet.

Thanks — Samir

--
Samir Shah
Director of Digital Transformation, Harbor Health
samir@harborhealth.com | (212) 555-0124

Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Forecasting commit probability & approval path

Thanks Samir — appreciate the color. Quick responses and plan: 

A) Pricing deliverables (we will send both items by EOD tomorrow):
- One-page cost summary (low/mid/high token profiles -> $/1M -> monthly cost)
- 3-tier pilot/commercial pricing PDF (attached: redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf) — pilot tier shows an illustrative 25–30% discount for a time-boxed 3-month pilot that commits to a minimum monthly token usage.

B) Procurement paths
- Pilot < $25k/month: we can offer a prepay credit card path to avoid full PO.
- Pilot between $25k–$75k/month: excused PO with executive sponsor + finance signoff (shorter lead time).
- >$75k/month: full procurement lane, expect 6–8 week lead time.

C) MAP & legal
- I’ll draft a short MAP with milestones and handoffs (SE success metrics, procurement checkpoint, legal review). If you want, I can coordinate a 15m call with our legal lead to accelerate any SOW questions.

Would you and Lena be available tomorrow (Mon) for a 20m call to walk the one-page sheet with finance? If not, we’ll send the artifacts and follow up.

Thanks — Vanessa

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Forecasting commit probability & approval path (internal)

Vanessa / Marissa — quick internal note before we send the finalized artifacts to Harbor: 

- SE will produce a tight per-1M-token sensitivity table capturing three scenarios: optimistic (high KV cache, batching), base (moderate cache), conservative (no cache). I’ll include the assumed average request tokens and effective tokens after batching.
- I’ll also map recommended inference levers (batch size, kv-cache TTL, quantization level) and the expected $/1M delta for each lever so finance can see where cost comes from.
- Deliverable ETA: draft cost sheet + recommended MAP by Tue 48 hours (EOD PDT).

If Marissa can surface any historical benchmarks from similar healthcare pilots (token counts or trial retention rates) I can bake that into the scenarios.

Thanks — Karthik
